_about: The larry template's workflows. Like config/workflows.json they are built in the UI (GHL has no workflow API, trap T4), from out/ui-checklist.md, all in Draft; verify checks each one by name.

Steps follow the source build as built, including its later changes: ad leads into the client's own pipeline, alerts to named users, a Mon-Fri sending window for REACT, SMS steps held until A2P. Source: spec/10-larry-template.md.
customer_facing: true = it emails or texts a lead, a customer or a partner. It stays Draft until a person switches it on after the client's go. Copy: out/template-copy.md.

programs.title: Speed to lead (STL)
rules: Every Internal Notification goes to Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}. Never "All users" (trap T10).
Reply and call tasks go to ${tpl.assistant_email}. GHL due dates are whole days, so "within 1 hour" goes in the task title and the task is due today.
Time window on both sending workflows: ${tpl.stl_window_text}.
Leads land in ${tpl.lead_pipeline} at ${tpl.lead_stage}. Ask the client where ad leads go BEFORE building: the source build was rebuilt when its leads moved to the client's own pipeline.

programs.title: Database reactivation (REACT)
rules: Segment workflows have no trigger: contacts are enrolled from the segment's smart list by bulk action, only on the client's go, one segment at a time.
Every segment workflow: Stop on response ON; Allow re-entry OFF; Allow multiple opportunities OFF; time window ${tpl.window_text}; unsubscribe link on every email.
Every Internal Notification goes to Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}. Tasks go to ${tpl.assistant_email}.
Email bodies go in through the editor's </> source view, one paragraph per block with a gap between them; otherwise the lines run together.

programs.title: Partner emails (AFF)
rules: This layer sits on the standard partner build: partner deals live in ${derived.names.recruiting} (before signing) and ${derived.names.lifecycle} (after), named {{contact.email}}; the partner's type, tier and referral count are the standard fields.
Every email is an email template first (Marketing -> Emails -> Templates), named "AFF - <workflow> - <email>", then picked in the Send Email step.
Email only until A2P is approved and the contact has SMS consent. ${tpl.sms_text}
No sending window was set on the source build's AFF workflows. Add ${tpl.window_text} if the client wants one.
Every Internal Notification goes to Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}.

workflows.name: STL | Ad Lead - Instant Response
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It texts and emails every new ad lead within a minute.
workflows.trigger: ${tpl.lead_trigger}. If leads also arrive through a website form, add a second trigger: Form submitted -> that form (ask the client).
settings: Stop on response: OFF (the instant reply goes out regardless)
steps: If / else "Already contacted?": contact has tag stl:contacted -> END. Otherwise continue.
Add tag: ${tpl.source_tag}, stl:new.
Update contact field: stl_status -> new; stl_first_touch_at -> today (Dynamic -> Right now -> Date).
Create opportunity: pipeline ${tpl.lead_pipeline}, stage ${tpl.lead_stage}, name "{{contact.name}} - Ad Lead", source {{contact.source}}, allow duplicates OFF.
Assign to user: ${tpl.assistant_email}, only if the contact has no owner yet.
Send SMS: STL SMS 01.
Wait 1 minute.
Send Email: STL Email 01.

Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}): subject "New ad lead: {{contact.name}}"; body "New ad lead: {{contact.name}} · {{contact.phone}} · {{contact.email}} · Form: {{contact.source}} · Instant SMS + email sent. {{contact.url}}".
Internal notification (SMS, Particular user: ${tpl.owner_email}): "New ad lead: {{contact.name}} {{contact.phone}}".
Remove tag stl:new; add tag stl:contacted; stl_status -> contacted.
Wait 2 minutes.
Add to workflow: STL | Ad Lead - Follow-Up Ladder.

steps.text: If / else: contact has tag src:partner-referral -> Remove tag ${tpl.source_tag} (a partner referral handed over by the partner layer is not an ad lead).

workflows.test: Enroll an @example.com contact with a phone no other contact uses (trap T18). Expect stl:contacted, stl_status contacted, one deal at ${tpl.lead_stage} in ${tpl.lead_pipeline}, the alert, and the contact in the Follow-Up Ladder. Run it twice: the second run ends at "Already contacted?".

workflows.name: STL | Ad Lead - Follow-Up Ladder
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It texts and emails the lead over 7 days.
workflows.trigger: None: contacts are added by STL | Ad Lead - Instant Response.
settings: Goal: Contact tag added stl:quick-app-complete -> the Complete branch (add the client's own "application finished" form as a second goal event if there is one)
steps: Wait 15 minutes.
If / else "Replied yet?": contact has tag stl:replied -> END.
Send SMS: STL SMS 02.
Wait 1 day.
Send Email: STL Email 02.
Wait 1 day.
Send SMS: STL SMS 03.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: STL Email 03.
Add task: "Call {{contact.name}} - no response to 4 touches", assigned to ${tpl.assistant_email}, due today.
Wait 3 days.
Send SMS: STL SMS 04.
Add tag: stl:no-response, react:segment-${tpl.unfinished_app_segment} (feeds the unfinished-application reactivation segment); stl_status -> no-response.

Complete branch (goal hit): add tag stl:handoff-${tpl.sender_slug}; stl_status -> quick-app-complete; Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}) "Quick app complete: {{contact.name}}"; Find opportunity (pipeline ${tpl.lead_pipeline}, the contact's open deal), then Update opportunity -> stage ${tpl.app_done_stage}. END.
workflows.test: With the waits set to 1 minute on a test copy: an @example.com contact gets SMS 02 to SMS 04, the call task, then stl:no-response. Adding stl:quick-app-complete mid-way jumps to Complete and moves the deal to ${tpl.app_done_stage}.

workflows.name: STL | Inbound Reply Router
workflows.trigger: Customer replied (SMS and email). Filters: contact has tag stl:contacted AND does not have tag stl:replied.
steps: Add tag stl:replied; stl_status -> replied.
Remove from workflow: STL | Ad Lead - Follow-Up Ladder.
${tpl.replied_stage_step}
Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}): "Reply from {{contact.name}}: {{message.body}} · {{contact.url}}".
Add task: "Reply to {{contact.name}} within 1 hour", assigned to ${tpl.assistant_email}, due today.
workflows.test: Reply to the test contact's STL email: stl:replied is added, the ladder stops, the alert and the task arrive.

workflows.name: REACT | Segment ${item.num} - ${item.name}
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It texts and emails past contacts over 14 days.
workflows.trigger: None: enrolled by bulk action from the smart list "REACT | ${item.num} - ${item.name}".
steps: If / else "Safety": contact has tag react:excluded -> END.
Add tag react:sent; remove tag react:queued; react_last_touch_at -> today.
Send Email: sequence "${item.sequence}", Email Day 0.
Wait 3 days.
Send Email: sequence "${item.sequence}", Email Day 3.
Wait 4 days.
Wait 7 days.
Send Email: sequence "${item.sequence}", Email Day 14.
Add tag react:not-now.
Wait 60 days.
Add to workflow: REACT | Re-entry - Check-in.
workflows.test: Enroll one @example.com contact tagged react:segment-${item.num}, with every wait at 1 minute on a test copy: each message arrives in order; a reply stops it and the REACT Reply Router fires.

workflows.name: REACT | Re-entry - Check-in
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It emails a contact 60 days after the sequence or a "not now" reply.
workflows.trigger: None: contacts are added by the segment workflows and the REACT Reply Router.
steps: Send Email: REACT Re-entry email (one email).
workflows.test: Add the test contact by hand: one email arrives.

workflows.name: REACT | Reply Router
workflows.trigger: Customer replied (SMS and email). Filters: contact has tag react:sent AND does not have tag react:replied.
steps: Add tag react:replied.
Remove from workflow: ${tpl.segment_workflow_names}, REACT | Re-entry - Check-in.
Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}): "Reactivation reply from {{contact.name}} ({{contact.react_segment}}): {{message.body}} · {{contact.url}}".

If / else on the reply text ("contains" any of): Stop = stop, unsubscribe, remove, don't contact, don’t contact, do not contact; Not now = not now, later, next year, maybe, busy; Wrong person = wrong, not me, no longer, retired, sold; Interested = everything else (the last branch).
Stop: Set DND, all channels; add tag react:do-not-contact. END.
Not now: add tag react:not-now; Wait 60 days; Add to workflow REACT | Re-entry - Check-in. END.
Wrong person: add tag react:do-not-contact. END.

Interested: add tag react:interested; Create opportunity in ${tpl.lead_pipeline} at ${tpl.lead_stage}, name "{{contact.name}} - Reactivation", source "Reactivation {{contact.react_segment}}", allow duplicates OFF; Add task "Reactivation reply - call {{contact.name}} within 2 hours", assigned to ${tpl.assistant_email}, due today. END.
workflows.test: Reply "stop", "maybe later", "wrong person" and "yes, tell me more" from four test contacts: each lands in its branch. Matching is "contains", so "sold" also matches "unsold": check real replies before go-live.

workflows.name: AFF | Call Booked
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It emails the partner a booking confirmation.
settings: Allow re-entry: ON (a partner can book again)
steps: Send Email: AFF - Call Booked - Confirmation (right after the trigger).
Add tag aff:call-booked.

Create opportunity: ${derived.names.recruiting} at Booked, name {{contact.email}}, allow duplicates OFF. Then Find opportunity (same pipeline, Opportunity Name = {{contact.email}}) and Update opportunity -> stage Booked, so a deal that already exists moves too (trap T14).
Remove from workflow: AFF | Partner Nurture - Every Other Day, ${tpl.outreach_workflow_names}.
Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}): "Partner call booked: {{contact.name}}", with Partner Type, the source and the last message.

steps.text: Wait until 1 hour before the appointment, then Send SMS: AFF call reminder (contacts with SMS consent only).

workflows.test: Book the partner calendar as an @example.com contact: the confirmation email, aff:call-booked, the deal at Booked and the alert. Check that {{appointment.start_time}} renders in the email.

workflows.name: AFF | Call No-Show
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It emails the partner a new booking link.
workflows.trigger: Appointment status changed to No-show, calendar ${derived.names.calendar}.
settings: Allow re-entry: OFF (the re-offer goes once)
steps: Add tag aff:no-show.
Send Email: AFF - Call Booked - No-show re-offer.
workflows.test: Mark the test booking No-show: aff:no-show and one re-offer email.

workflows.name: AFF | Reply Router
workflows.trigger: Two triggers. Customer replied, filters: tag aff:signed AND not aff:replied. Customer replied, filters: tag aff:outreach-sent AND not aff:replied.
steps: Add tag aff:replied.
Internal notification (Email, Particular users: ${tpl.alert_list}): "Partner reply from {{contact.name}}: {{message.body}} · {{contact.url}}".

If / else on the reply text ("contains" any of): Stop = stop, unsubscribe; Not interested = not interested, no thanks, covered; Comp question = commission, pay, split, comp, %; Other = everything else (the last branch).
Stop: Set DND, all channels; add tag aff:declined. END.
Not interested: add tag aff:declined. END.
Comp question: Add task "Comp question from {{contact.name}}", assigned to ${tpl.owner_email}, due in 1 day. The approved no-numbers reply is in the copy. END.
Other: Add task "Partner reply - respond to {{contact.name}} within 2 hours", assigned to ${tpl.assistant_email}, due today. Reply snippets are in the copy. END.
No deal-stage moves here (left out in the source build): the person who handles the reply moves the deal.
workflows.test: Reply to a test outreach email with "not interested", "what's the commission?" and "sounds good": each lands in its branch with its task.

workflows.name: AFF | Partner Nurture - Every Other Day
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It emails every new partner 8 times over 14 days.
steps: Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 1 · Day 0.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 2 · Day 2.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 3 · Day 4.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 4 · Day 6.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 5 · Day 8.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 6 · Day 10.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 7 · Day 12.
Wait 2 days.
Send Email: AFF - Nurture - Email 8 · Day 14.
workflows.test: Tag a test partner aff:signed with the waits at 1 minute on a test copy: 8 emails in order; a reply stops them.

workflows.name: AFF | Partner Check-In - 30/60
workflows.customerFacingWhy: It emails partners at 30 and 60 days.
steps: Wait 30 days.
If / else: Referrals Sent is greater than 0 -> "Has referred" branch; else -> "No referral yet" branch.
Has referred: Wait 30 days; Send Email: AFF - Check-In - Day 60. END.
No referral yet: Send Email: AFF - Check-In - Day 30; Wait 30 days; Send Email: AFF - Check-In - Day 60. END.
Nothing increments Referrals Sent automatically (the source build was the same): whoever confirms a referral updates it.
workflows.test: With the waits at 1 minute on a test copy: a partner with Referrals Sent 0 gets Day 30 then Day 60; with 1 gets Day 60 only.

workflows.name: AFF | Outreach - ${item.name}
steps: Add tag aff:outreach-sent.
Send Email: AFF - Outreach ${item.name} - Email 1.

steps.text: Send SMS: SMS 1 (contacts with SMS consent only).

steps: Wait 3 days.
Send Email: AFF - Outreach ${item.name} - Email 2 (subject "re: " + the Email 1 subject, so it reads as a reply in the same thread).
Wait 4 days.
Send Email: AFF - Outreach ${item.name} - Email 3.
Wait 5 days.
Send Email: AFF - Outreach ${item.name} - Email 4.

steps.text: Send SMS: SMS 4 (contacts with SMS consent only).

workflows.test: Tag an @example.com contact that has a company name aff:queue-${item.key}: aff:outreach-sent and Email 1 arrive; a reply stops the sequence and the AFF Reply Router fires.
